name: Barbados
summary: Ultramarine, gold and ultramarine vertical bands with a black broken trident in the centre. The trident comes from the colonial badge, which showed Britannia holding a trident; breaking its shaft symbolised the break from colonial rule.
origin: A competition for an independence flag received over 1,000 entries. Grantley Prescod's design was chosen, and the flag was raised at independence on 30 November 1966.
The colonial badge of Barbados showed Britannia with a trident. The national flag keeps only the head of the trident, its shaft broken off.

colors.name: Gold
colors.meaning: The sand of the island's beaches.

symbols.name: Broken trident
symbols.description: The head of a trident, with its shaft broken.
symbols.meaning: The break with Barbados's colonial past; the three points stand for the three principles of democracy: government of, for and by the people.

history.label: Barbados
history.note: Kept when Barbados became a republic in 2021.

facts: Barbados became a republic on 30 November 2021, exactly 55 years after independence, without changing its flag.
Its trident is the only one on a national flag.
Saint Vincent and the Grenadines also has a blue-gold-green vertical tricolour.
clues: Blue, gold and blue vertical bands with a black trident head.
Its trident's broken shaft symbolises a break from colonial rule.
Its country became a republic on its 55th independence anniversary.
